title: Pop a nonempty bridge stack
statement: Let $c$ be a compiled program, let $x$ be a bridge input word, and choose optional bridge states $q,q'$, a valid input-head position $p$, an assignment $st$ of stacks to the four stack names, and an output word. If the stack at a chosen name $k$ is $a::xs$, then applying the action that blanks the current cell of the work tape for $k$ and moves that tape's head one cell to the right, with successor state $q'$, gives the bridge configuration with state $q'$, the stack at $k$ replaced by $xs$, and the input-head position and output unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: An assignment $st$ of stacks to the four stack names
A symbol $a$ and stack tail $xs$ with $st(k)=a::xs$
replaced:
Suppose that in a bridge configuration the stack assigned to a name $k$ is nonempty,
with top symbol $a$ above a tail $xs$.  Then the one-tape action on the tape of $k$
that blanks the current cell and moves that head one cell to the right, passing to a
control state $q'$, transforms the configuration into the bridge configuration with
control state $q'$ whose assignment replaces the stack at $k$ by $xs$, the input
position and output unchanged.
